transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-05-18 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~42 mins
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sara Velasquez (Latitude), James Park (Latitude), Rina Kapoor (Latitude)

Summary:
Quick renewal & expansion check-in: Latitude is evaluating a Dedicated reserved pool + adding eu-west region and discussing contract term extension (12 -> 24 months) for better unit pricing. Talked through capacity sizing, cost/latency tradeoffs, security/compliance requirements, and next steps for benchmarks and updated pricing.

Topics:
- Capacity bump from 50 to 150 concurrent sessions (estimate)
- Add EU region (eu-west) and plan for APAC later
- Contract extension incentives and discount tiers
- Security: KMS, SOC2, VPC peering, audit logs
- Pilot/benchmark timeline and success criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, um, thanks for joining. Quick kickoff  thanks for adjusting the time. I'm Maya Chen, AE at Redwood, with Liam on the line, our solutions engineer.
[00:22] Sara: Hi Maya, hi Liam  Sara here. Thanks, we'll keep it tight, Rina's gotta hop on at 3:30 PT.
[00:30] Liam: Hey all, looks like we're good to go. I have the capacity numbers and the perf deck ready to reference.
[02:15] Maya: Quick agenda, confirm what you're looking to expand, make sure pricing and terms align, and plan the benchmark window. So, Sara, can you remind us of current usage and the ask?
[02:45] Sara: Sure  currently on Hosted, about 50 concurrent realtime sessions for our fraud chat flows, 1.2M tokens/day. We're approaching a seasonal spike and the product team wants predictable latency; they asked about Dedicated to reduce jitter and have better isolation. We're also starting EU pilots in Q3 so need eu-west region support.
[03:20] James: And finance chimes in  we're looking at 12 month contract today but open to 24 months if unit price drops; Rina will confirm later.
[05:10] Liam: Right, from technical side Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity, predictable throughput. We recommend a pool sized for peak concurrency plus headroom; for 150 concurrent we'd look at a 4-6 GPU pool depending on model and quantization. There's an autoscale burst option too.
[06:02] Sara: When you say 4-6 GPUs, baseline cost looks higher than hosted  what's the unit economics tradeoff? We care about latency under 200ms for short prompts.
[06:35] Maya: Good callout. The trade is predictable latency and lower tail latencies vs hosted where multi-tenant noise can increase p95. Per-token cost can drop if you commit spend/longer term and use caching/batching. We'll share a model-specific cost projection.
[08:00] Rina (joined): Sorry I'm late, had a back-to-back. Rina Kapoor, CFO. Quick: want the numbers and a clear migration plan  also need SOC2 compliance proof and KMS for key separation.
[08:30] Maya: Absolutely. We have SOC 2 Type II and can integrate with your KMS/HSM. We'll attach the security whitepaper and the audit attestation.
[09:10] James: For eu-west, is data residency enforced, or is it just serving region? Our legal team requires PII at rest to stay in EU.
[09:45] Liam: We can pin model serving to eu-west and ensure storage is regional. For Private deployments we can do customer-managed VPC; for Dedicated in hosted we have region-specific storage and can enable customer-controlled encryption keys. There might be small differences in log routing that we can show.
[11:05] Sara: About benchmarks  we want a test simulating our production prompts, 90% short form, 10% long context of 4k tokens. Can Redwood support a KV-cache warmup and steady-state run?
[11:45] Liam: Yes, we'll plan a multi-day run: cold start, warm cache, and sustained load. We'll instrument p50/p95/p99 and token cost. I'll share the test harness and sample scripts.
[13:30] James: Any limitation on model variants? We use a LLaMA-based open model tuned for our data; we care about quantization compatibility and performance.
[14:10] Liam: We support several open models and quantization profiles; some models have better kernel paths on certain GPU families. We'll map your model to recommended instance types. There may be minor perf delta between 8-bit quant and fp16, but the cost savings often justify it.
[16:00] Rina: On pricing  what discount tiers do we get for committed capacity? We're considering a 24-month commit if unit drops 20-30%.
[16:35] Maya: Our standard is a sliding scale: 12 month at X% off, 24 month at higher discount; with reserved Dedicated capacity you get better per-token rates and lower overage multipliers. I'll produce a pricing sheet with tiered examples for your expected 150 concurrent baseline.
[18:20] Sara: Also curious about burst  we want to absorb spikes without throttling. How does autoscale interact with committed pools?
[18:55] Liam: There's a burst buffer that can be used; if you exceed reserved capacity, requests can spill to a burst pool billed at a higher rate. You can set policy: failover to hosted model or queue. We'll show sample policies.
[20:30] James: Security checklist  SSO, SAML, RBAC, audit logs retention. Can we set retention to 7 years if needed? That's a legal ask for certain markets.
[21:05] Maya: Audit logs retention is configurable as an add-on. SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning are supported; RBAC can be mapped to your groups. We'll list limits and costs.
[22:50] Rina: On contract term, if we go 24 months and commit to a baseline spend, can we include a performance SLA on p95 latency?
[23:18] Maya: Yes we can include SLA language for dedicated pools with clear SLOs and credits for breach. We'll draft proposed language in the contract addendum.
[24:45] Sara: One more technical  we use prefix caching a lot. Does Redwood preserve KV cache across warm restarts? We had inconsistencies on another provider.
[25:10] Liam: We have KV-cache persistence features; we can persist and restore cache for steady-state. Wording might differ but functionally you'll see reduced token compute on warm restarts. I'll note that in the benchmark doc.
[27:00] James: Network  we'll need firewall / IP allowlist, and potential VPC peering. Any single IP range we need to open?
[27:35] Liam: We'll provide a small set of egress/ingress CIDR blocks. For private/VPC options we can do peering and push NAT through your VPC.
[29:10] Rina: If we sign a 24-month, what's the exit clause if we outgrow the reserved pool or need to move to Private on-prem?
[29:45] Maya: We typically allow one re-sizing per quarter with pro-rated changes. For Private migrations there are migration services and credits we can discuss; we'll add migration terms to the contact.
[31:00] Sara: Ok  success criteria for the pilot: p95 < 250ms for short prompts, p99 measurable and within 2x baseline, cost per 1k tokens under target, and security sign-off.
[31:35] Maya: Perfect, we'll put that in writing in the SOW.
[33:00] Liam: I'll run through the tentative benchmark plan: day 1 cold starts, day 2 warm-up + KV cache warm, day 3 steady-state 8 hours. We'll capture JSON logs and perf traces.
[34:15] James: Please include the exact prompts and a redacted dataset so we can run locally too.
[34:45] Liam: Yes  sample harness and scrubbed dataset.
[35:30] Rina: Financial ask  show the impact of 12 vs 24 month on ARR and monthly burn. We'll need a side-by-side.
[35:55] Maya: We'll produce a 12/24 comparison sheet with committed baseline and burst overage scenarios.
[37:20] Sara: Any blockers we should know about? We have a compliance review scheduled 2027-06-02. If we have security docs before then, we can fast-track procurement.
[37:50] Maya: We'll prioritize the SOC2 attestation and KMS integration guide; Liam will also send network checklist.
[39:10] James: Competitors  we ran a quick eval of Anthropic endpoints for latency; they were good but cost was higher. We like Redwood's batching options.
[40:05] Liam: Thanks. One note  some transcription earlier: K V cache spelled out sometimes in notes as K V cash which is fine but we'll attach the tech sheet.
[40:35] Maya: Recap of next steps: 1) Maya sends updated pricing and contract language, 2) Liam shares benchmark plan + network checklist, 3) Customer confirms baseline and sends PII data flow diagram.
[41:10] Rina: That sounds good. We'll aim to decide on commit level by next Friday.
[41:30] Maya: Great thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to the security docs and pricing.

References/links mentioned:
- Pricing spreadsheet (to be sent)
- Security whitepaper and SOC2 attestation (link to be included)
- Benchmark harness + scripts (to be shared by Liam)

End of transcript.
